chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The righteous child is an aromatic flower from God, distributed by Him among His servants. And indeed, my two aromatic flowers from this world are al-Hasan and al-Husayn. I named them both by the names of two grandsons from the Children of Israel: Shabbar and Shabbir.'

key_terms.رَيْحَانَةٌ: A sweet-smelling herb or aromatic flower; used metaphorically for a beloved child who brings joy and blessing
key_terms.سِبْطَيْنِ: Two grandsons; referring specifically to grandsons from a daughter's lineage in Semitic usage
key_terms.شَبَّر وَشَبِير: Arabicized forms of Shibr and Shibir (Hebrew: Shever/Shabbir), names of grandsons of Prophet Musa through his daughter

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about al-Hasan and al-Husayn being his two fragrant flowers from the world?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) describes a righteous child as a fragrant flower distributed by God among His servants, then specifically identifies al-Hasan and al-Husayn as his own two 'flowers' from this world. He further reveals that their names were chosen to correspond with the names Shabbar and Shabbir — the grandsons of Prophet Musa (Moses) in the Israelite tradition — establishing a sacred lineage that spans prophethood. This hadith is situated in Al-Kafi's chapter on the merits of children, placing the Imam's grandchildren at the pinnacle of that virtue.
